identification.name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 (DMLS, Heat Treated)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied as gas-atomised powder for direct metal laser sintering (DMLS/SLM), printed into near-net-shape parts then post-machined as needed. See the wrought Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Annealed) and (Grade 5) STA entries in this database for conventional bar/sheet/plate stock.
identification.notes: Sourced from EOS's official Titanium Ti64 Grade 5 Material Data Sheet, EOS M 290 | 40 µm process. Unlike Maraging 300 and 17-4 PH also in this database, AM (additive manufacturing) Ti-6Al-4V's condition story is different: the as-built state is a brittle, needle-like (acicular alpha-prime) microstructure from rapid solidification with poor ductility — EOS's document doesn't report as-built mechanical properties at all and explicitly recommends heat treatment, not to increase strength via aging (there is none here) but to relieve residual stress and improve ductility. "Heat Treated" (this entry) means a stress-relief anneal only: 120 min (±30 min) at 800°C (±10°C) in vacuum, furnace/argon cooled — EOS's standard recommendation. The source also reports a "Heat Treated + HIP" (Hot Isostatic Pressing) condition for the most fatigue-critical applications, with notably lower yield/tensile strength (~900–1010 MPa vs. ~970–1010 MPa here) but slightly better elongation and reduction of area — worth a separate entry if HIP-specific properties matter for a project. Reported separately for vertical and horizontal build orientation: yield 1010/970 MPa, tensile 1080/1080 MPa, elongation 15%/14%, reduction of area ≥25% both — stored values are simple averages. Density (≥4.4 g/cm³, ISO (International Organization for Standardization) 3369, measured on the built specimen) closely matches the wrought alloy's ~4.43 g/cm³, consistent with a well-optimized, nearly fully-dense print (source reports <0.1% average defect percentage). Bulk/condition-independent physical properties (Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, thermal conductivity, specific heat, melting point, electrical conductivity) are reused from the wrought Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Annealed) entry in this database, since EOS's datasheet doesn't report them and they aren't expected to vary meaningfully between wrought and AM processing of the same base alloy. CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) is from EOS's own table (ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) E228), preferred over the wrought entry's value since it's AM-specific. Shear strength derived via von Mises: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 1080/1.732 ≈ 624 MPa. Fatigue strength (heat treated, ISO 12107 statistical estimate at 1×10⁷ cycles): 595 MPa — not stored as a formal S-N curve point since only one cycle count is given.

typical_usage: High strength-to-weight DMLS/SLM-printed parts needing titanium's corrosion resistance and biocompatibility combined with AM geometric freedom: aerospace brackets and fittings, medical implants and surgical guides, and lightweight lattice/topology-optimized structures not achievable with wrought stock. Requires access to a metal AM system and a post-print stress-relief furnace cycle — as-built parts are notably more brittle until heat treated.
